title: How Syria is balancing public anger, regional stability after Jordan's strikes
gist: Jordan carried out airstrikes in southern Syria's Daraa and Suwayda governorates that Amman says killed at least 20 Islamic State members in retaliation for an Oct. 23 church funeral massacre in Karak, while Damascus says seven civilians, including children, died. Syrian FM Asaad al-Shaibani visited victims' families, framing a balancing act between domestic anger and regional stability.

insights.so_what: Signals Jordan's willingness to project force across its northern border, raising cross-border escalation risk in southern Syria.

insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
